title: Home Telemonitoring of Weight and Symptoms in Heart Failure: A Randomized Trial
abstract: A randomized trial of 380 heart failure patients compared daily home weight telemonitoring with usual care, reporting 30-day readmission as the primary endpoint.
rationale: Adult HF population, RPM intervention, RCT design, reports readmission outcome as required.

title: Perspectives of Family Caregivers on Remote Monitoring Devices: A Focus Group Study
abstract: This qualitative focus group study explored family caregivers' perceptions of remote monitoring devices used by elderly heart failure patients, with no quantitative outcomes reported.
rationale: Purely qualitative with no quantitative readmission data, fails outcome criterion.

title: Feasibility of a Wearable Patch Sensor in Neonatal Intensive Care
abstract: A feasibility study of a wearable vital-sign patch sensor in neonates admitted to the NICU, unrelated to heart failure or adult populations.
rationale: Pediatric/neonatal population and unrelated condition, fails population criterion.

title: Retrospective Cohort Analysis of Telehealth Follow-Up and 90-Day Readmission in Heart Failure
abstract: A retrospective cohort study of 450 adult heart failure patients compared structured telehealth follow-up with standard care, reporting 90-day all-cause readmission rates.
rationale: Adult HF population, RPM/telehealth intervention, cohort design, reports readmission outcome.

title: Study Protocol: A Planned Trial of Remote Monitoring in Heart Failure (No Results Yet)
abstract: This protocol paper outlines the design of a future randomized trial on remote monitoring in heart failure; the trial has not yet been conducted and no results are available.
rationale: Protocol-only paper with no outcome data, fails study design/completeness criterion.
